title: Marriage calculator
subject: For a couple described by the user, compares taxes, benefits and net household income when living together against the combined income of two separate households. The income grid varies those household earnings; it is not a population distribution.

living_together.description: Two adults live together as one couple and household under the tax-benefit rules for the selected year, compared with the same adults living in separate households. The app keeps children with the first adult when separated; external specimens record their own child-allocation assumptions.

living_apart.description: The two adults live in separate households under the same tax-benefit rules, with household-specific earnings, children and housing arrangements.

ifs_scenario_a.description: IFS 2010–11 Scenario A: compare an existing mixed-sex couple with the same adults assessed as single people while remaining in the same household. Children stay with the woman; characteristics, income sources and asset ownership otherwise stay fixed.

ifs_scenario_b.description: IFS 2010–11 Scenario B: compare an existing mixed-sex couple with the same adults assessed as single people in separate single-adult households, with housing costs assigned from matched households. Children stay with the woman; characteristics, income sources and asset ownership otherwise stay fixed.

oecd_1998_hypothetical_couples.description: OECD WP76 section5: fixed-earnings hypothetical couples under 1998 UK tax-transfer rules, comparing married/cohabiting status with two separated single adults. Rent is divided equally; in the two-child cases each separated adult has custody of one child. The ten income configurations use primary- and secondary-earner earnings percentiles; money values are converted to 2007 euros using compensation-per-employee indices and exchange rates.

csj_2009_equivalised_comparison.description: CSJ Dynamic Benefits current-system 2009 snapshot: existing FRS couples compared with synthetic separation after equivalising income to allow for savings from living together. Material penalties concern a lower standard of living, not unadjusted combined cash transfers. The input survey is 2005/06; the publication does not supply an exact policy fiscal year.

calculator.reason: The live UK page computes taxes, benefits and net-income changes for the household the user enters, together and as two separate households, including an income-grid chart for that household. It publishes no fixed population count, fiscal cost, share or specimen-household estimate and reads no aggregate results file. The live HTML deployment ID dpl_6F85da9qGCBcVmpyNtGAY3Lwo9Ms matches the successful Vercel status on PolicyEngine/marriage commit 2864e4092d6a9dd259845fd76925878bcb69e852. At that commit app/MarriageApp.jsx initializes results to null and calculates on submission; lib/api.js computes the couple and two separate households through the runtime service, lib/countries.js selects /uk/calculate, and backend/uk.py accepts exactly one household. Code and deployment evidence URLs and hashes are recorded with the open_search checks; there is no results file to pin.
